absent: Architecture rewrite semantics for static call sites including tail handling.
Memory layout of static call key, site, module tracker, and trampoline key records.
Nature and ordering guarantees of the static call lock.
Module record fields for static call sites and tracepoint tables.
Tracepoint record fields including iterator, key, trampoline, extension, and faultable property.
Iterator behavior for multi probe dispatch and reader side dereference rules.
Numeric value of default probe priority and usable priority range.
RCU and SRCU progress, polling, and synchronize guarantees used by transition sampling.
Blocking notifier registration and delivery semantics and notifier return encoding.
Debug control value and logging behavior for probe dumps.

findings.text: Tracepoint service offers adding a probe callback with data and priority and removing by callback plus data. One priority form warns on duplicates, a may-exist form suppresses that warning, and a default form supplies a standard priority.
Tracepoint service offers subscribing and unsubscribing observers of module arrival and departure, replaying the current tracker set so late subscribers observe existing modules.
Tracepoint service offers iteration over tracepoints in a pointer range or in one module, invoking a caller callback per tracepoint and tolerating empty input.
Tracepoint service exposes a predicate reporting whether a module carries disqualifying taints outside the permitted staging and test related set.
Boot entry initializes core static call sites once, registers for module events only on first success path, and makes repeat invocation a no-op.
Static call module observer handles arrival by resolving and initializing module sites and departure by unlinking them, cleaning up after a failed arrival.
Tracepoint module observer accepts arrival and departure events for modules with tracepoints, ignores other lifecycle states, and is installed at early boot.
Early selftest entry exercises a test static call through unconfigured and two configured targets and checks each invocation yields the expected value.
Static call initialization requires sites ordered and grouped by key, marks sites residing in init memory, and requests architecture rewrite of every site toward its key current target.
A static call key uses a direct site reference for the base kernel and a per-module tracker list once modules use it, converting the direct form into an explicit list entry on first module use.
Module site fixup accepts only encoded addresses in kernel text, resolves trampoline addresses to keys through a dedicated table, preserves site flag bits, and rejects unresolvable sites.

Probe arrays are null terminated, contain no duplicate callback plus data pair, are ordered so higher priority entries precede lower priority entries, and exclude placeholder entries from the logical count.
Tracepoint dispatch uses direct call to the sole probe when exactly one probe exists and an iterator otherwise; synthetic events without a static key never update dispatch.
External enable and disable callbacks are invoked only on transitions that change enablement from disabled to enabled or back, with cleanup on failed addition.
A change of the first probe data across an update that keeps at least one probe records a deferred synchronization sample for the multi to single transition class.
Old probe storage is never freed synchronously; it is deferred through tasks-trace grace handling for faultable tracepoints and through SRCU otherwise.
Modules without tracepoints or with disallowed taints are ignored for tracking; tracked modules each own one list entry created on arrival and destroyed on departure.
Module departure requires quiescence of that module tracepoints, meaning no probe callbacks remain installed at going time.
Static call initialization and module arrival or departure hold CPU read protection outer and the static call lock inner.
Probe addition and removal and all public probe register and unregister wrappers serialize on a dedicated tracepoints mutex, which also guards protected access to the probe pointer.
The tracepoint module tracker list and notifier subscription changes serialize on a dedicated module list mutex, which callers must already hold when iterating one module tracepoints.
Probe storage couples a deferred-free header with a trailing variable length array of probe descriptors.
Transition synchronization state holds an RCU cookie, an SRCU cookie, and an ongoing flag, with one instance per transition class.
Selftest table entries associate an optional integer function with an input value and an expected result value.

Probe count states are empty, one, two, and many. Empty to one publishes then enables; one to two updates dispatch before publishing; removal from one disables before publishing empty; two to one publishes, waits, then narrows dispatch.
Each transition class moves between idle and sampling: sampling records RCU and SRCU progress markers, waiting honors them only when sampling is active and then returns to idle.
Key tracking moves from direct base reference to tracker list on first module use, then adds and removes one tracker per using module while preserving the base entry.
Module lifecycle handling distinguishes coming and going; coming installs tracking and notifies arrival, going notifies departure then validates quiescence, and unrelated states have no effect.
Static call paths fail cleanly on tracker allocation exhaustion and on failure to resolve a module trampoline address, with arrival failure triggering unlink rollback.
Probe management reports duplicate insertion, missing removal target, null callback, and allocation exhaustion as distinct errors rather than corrupting the array.

Removal under allocation pressure replaces targets with a no-op placeholder in place and keeps the old array; module unlink stops at the first unconverted key to avoid interpreting memory incorrectly.
Failure to initialize core static calls is fatal at boot; lingering probes at module departure and ignored tainted modules are treated as warnings or skips to avoid crashes.
Probe count classification exposes four ordered values representing zero, one, two, and three or more installed probes.
Deferred synchronization exposes two transition classes, one for empty to single oscillation and one for multi to single narrowing, plus a count of classes.
